what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 2: Are the walls of simply connected lattice regions connected through shared edges?. LANDED FIRST: origin/main is the science authority; read each named note as landed (git show origin/main:docs/<note>) before any PR branch, and where a PR's wording differs from the landed text, the landed text controls. Blocks 116-118 are OPEN hand-off PRs (#9159, #9160, #9162): read them on their branches (gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName; git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). They are by the supervisor's model family (Claude) and harvest Grok-refereed probes attempts; nothing in them is adopted. SETTING: block 117 (PR #9160) bounds the regions V around a site (V a finite face-connected set of Z^3 sites whose complement is face-connected) through the wall of V, the plaquettes between V and its complement; it imports that the wall is connected when plaquettes sharing a VERTEX count as adjacent (32 neighbours each, Mayer-Vietoris), and the probes attempt the-record-gas-chessboard-threshold a2 (#9034) notes that if walls were connected through shared EDGES (12 neighbours) the same certificate would give g near 1.2e-3 instead of 9/62500. Every wall of at most six cells is edge-connected (checked). TASK: (a) prove that the wall of every such V is connected through shared edges, or give a counterexample (the smallest you can find, e.g. two cubes touching along an edge inside V's closure); (b) if true, redo block 117's certificate exactly with the 12-neighbour tree count and state the new g* without contents and at (3,1,2); if false, state the weakest adjacency (vertex or edge plus a local repair) for which a connectedness theorem holds and its certificate. HIT: (a) settled with exact checks. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/edge-connected-walls-of-simply-connected-regions/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes AS LANDED ON MAIN (git show origin/main:<note>); use a PR branch (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName,state) only for a note that is not on main; any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
